react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight input metabolites resolved cleanly across three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms (RaMP multi-DB ORA, Mummichog m/z-direct, MetaboAnalystR PSEA). Four pathways achieved cross-paradigm consensus with rank ≤ 5 in at least two tools. Leukotriene A4 (KEGG:C00909) is the dominant driver, hitting Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) via MetaboAnalystR (rank 1, p=0.0807) and via Mummichog (rank 0, p=0.021), and also appearing in RaMP's broad Metabolism super-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-1430728). Norepinephrine (KEGG:C00547) independently drives Tyrosine metabolism (Mummichog rank 2) and Arachidonic acid metabolism (MetaboAnalystR rank 0, p=0.0771 for hsa00350 — the shared phenylalanine/tyrosine catabolism module), while simultaneously anchoring three G-protein coupled receptor signaling modules in RaMP (REACT:R-HSA-418594 G alpha(i) events, REACT:R-HSA-388396 GPCR downstream signaling, REACT:R-HSA-372790 Signaling by GPCR, all FDR ≤ 0.00175). Coumarin (KEGG:C05851) independently contributes to Xenobiotics metabolism (Mummichog) and to the same GPCR signaling clusters via structural complementarity in the ligand-binding pocket. The six resolved compounds form two biological stories: (1) inflammatory eicosanoid disruption via the leukotriene branch of arachidonic acid metabolism, and (2) monoamine/GPCR signaling perturbation anchored by norepinephrine and coumarin co-enrichment in GPCR ligand-binding pathways. All InChIKeys were reconciled to eight distinct block-14 clusters with no structural conflicts, confirming the signal is not a namespace artifact.
